A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Generative Omnimatte. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, moves, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-decomposition and object-removal results, quantitative evaluations in Tables 1–2, and ablations in Figure 9 and Tables 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds CogVideoX-based Casper demonstrations, a prompt-sensitivity comparison, and runtime results.

M1.justification: Appendix A adds a CogVideoX-based, diffusion-transformer version of Casper trained on the same data. This introduces an alternative model backbone; the original Lumiere-based removal model, trimask procedure, and RGBA optimization remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Figure 15 adds a limited test scenario with deliberately unrelated textual conditioning, comparing an empty-scene prompt with a crowded-rock-concert prompt on beach footage. The four training-data categories and ten-scene Movie/Kubric benchmark remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in the existing quantitative and visual comparisons is unchanged. New Appendix E adds runtime comparisons against original Lumiere-Inpainting and OmnimatteRF; v1 reported Casper's inference time without these runtime comparisons.

E3.justification: The added CogVideoX experiment uses 85-frame, 384×672 videos and 50 DDIM steps without classifier-free guidance. Figure 15 introduces paired prompt conditions. These are additional experimental settings; the original Lumiere sampling protocol, benchmark metrics, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a qualitative prompt-sensitivity test in Figure 15 and computational-cost analysis in Appendix E. The existing training-data, mask-condition, and RGB-optimization ablations remain intact. The occluded-dog demonstration is retained as Figure 14, formerly Figure 13.

E5.justification: Both versions specify a fixed inference seed of 0 and state that seeds are not cherry-picked. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical results, including the proposed method's average PSNR of 38.38 and LPIPS of 0.020. New results include CogVideoX removal examples, prompt-dependent artifacts, 66-second CogVideoX sampling, and estimated full-pipeline runtimes of 49 minutes serially or 35 minutes with multiple TPUs. These timings do not establish a controlled same-setting speed gain.

T1.justification: The attention-response definition, trimask formulation, compositing equations, reconstruction and sparsity losses, and appendix alpha-supervision formulation are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding claims retain the same scope: generative video-layer decomposition, object-effect association, dynamic-background handling, and completion of occluded content using a small curated training set.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion explains sensitivity to unrelated prompts, hypothesizes synthetic-to-real discrepancies behind similar-object failures, and describes the tradeoff between Object-Paste background preservation and effect removal. It also clarifies why detail transfer is conservative and proposes input-aware super-resolution as future work.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the third-party CogVideoX-Fun code/model source, supplies its sampling configuration and A100 timing, and documents TPU memory, inference batch size, stage timings, and parallelization for the original pipeline. It also clarifies full finetuning. Dataset and generation-script release remain promises rather than newly reported releases.

R1.justification: v2 adds Magic Fixup and Preserve Your Own Correlation to the references and broadens the related-work discussion of image-based object-effect removal. CogVideoX was already cited in v1; its new experimental use is a separate change. Venue and reference-number updates do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments, Additional Discussions and Runtime appendix sections, expands the training discussion, and slightly rewrites related work. The main narrative remains largely unchanged. The new CogVideoX paragraph contains a citation mismatch: it cites [56], whereas CogVideoX is reference [58].

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 13 and 15 for CogVideoX results and prompt sensitivity, retains the former Figure 13 as Figure 14, and rearranges appendix text and table spacing. Existing main-paper figures and the structures of Tables 1–4 remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The public-backbone demonstration, prompt-sensitivity evidence, clearer limitations, and detailed runtime/resource reporting improve practical reproducibility and assessment of applicability. These are bounded gains: the original benchmark evidence is unchanged, the new backbone is evaluated qualitatively, and runtime comparisons lack matched settings. The small citation error does not outweigh these benefits.
